thread:
anya: Quick follow-up to the RFC — we need to decide where RBAC checks live for dashboard queries. current thinking: centralized authz layer in query proxy vs pushdown filters to DB/storage.
kevin: Short version: proxy-authz is simpler for rollouts but hurts cacheability and increases fanout. pushdown can reduce returned rows but complicates permissions model.
maria: Can we define a narrow contract so pushdown is only allowed for 'tenant-scoped' dashboards? that keeps most dashboards simple.
kevin: That helps. tradeoffs:
• proxy: single place for audit logs + uniform error messages
• pushdown: better per-request latency and lower token costs when we avoid row filtering at app layer
samir: +1 on the audit logs point. For several enterprise customers we need KMS-backed auditability and easy tracing of which principal saw what.
lia: note: pushdown means we need to surface a sanitized predicate API to model owners, otherwise they can infer tenancy boundaries. security risk.
anya: good call. proposal: default=proxy-authz, allow pushdown via an explicit opt-in flag on the dashboard config (admin only). must pass through a validator service that only allows a safe predicate subset.
kevin: Implementation sketch:
```
dashboard.config {
  authz: "proxy" | "pushdown:validated"
  pushdown_predicate: "<expr>"  # validated by authz-validator
}
```
maria: what about caching? proxy-authz prevents sharing query results across tenants unless we do tokenized caches.
samir: we could introduce a cache key normalization that includes a short-lived authz-hash for proxy mode. still means cache miss rate goes up for multi-tenant dashboards.
lia: For SLOs: proxy adds ~5-12ms median depending on lookup complexity. pushdown reduces median but increases variance when storage needs to evaluate complex predicates.
kevin: Ops-wise, rollouts: start with proxy-only. expose telemetry: authz-time, filter-pushdown-rate, cache-hit-by-authz-hash. We can schedule a 2-week experiment with a few internal dashboards.
anya: Action items:
- @kevin: add telemetry counters + trace tags (authz.method)
- @maria: write validator service proto (predicate grammar)
- @samir: check legal/audit requirements for storing authz-hash in logs
- @lia: write threat model notes for pushdown
kevin: I'll post a tiny benchmark script (local) that runs 1k dashboard queries with both modes.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-platform/authz-metrics v0.1 -> canary at 2026-04-12T03:00Z :truck:
maria: quick question — if a dashboard uses mixed data sources (some tenant-aware, some global), do we allow pushdown only on the tenant-aware legs?
anya: yes, pushdown only applies to sources that explicitly declare 'tenant_key' and opt-in in their connector config.
kevin: last thought — we should avoid pushing complex SQL generation into connectors. keep pushdown predicates as conjunctive, simple ops (eq, in, lt/gt) to keep planning predictable.
lia: agreed. that also makes validator simpler.
anya: ok if i draft a short RFC follow-up with the opt-in path and timeline later today?
maria: please do. i'll review and add the proto sketch.
kevin: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
